questions.question: The primary area of the residual limb used for weight bearing in a transtibial prosthesis is the:

options.B: Distal end of the residual limb

questions.explanation: The patellar tendon-bearing socket loads the patellar tendon and other pressure-tolerant areas; the distal end and fibular head are relieved.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed.Pg. 239

questions.question: Cock up splint is used in the management of:
questions.explanation: A cock-up splint holds the wrist in extension in radial nerve palsy (wrist drop).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Von Rosen splint is used in:
questions.explanation: Von Rosen splint is used for congenital (developmental) dislocation of the hip.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: For a patient having foot drop the orthosis recommended is:
questions.explanation: An ankle-foot orthosis is the standard device for foot drop.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Toe raising spring is indicated in:

options.D: Knee flexion deformity Physiotherapy in Ortho

questions.explanation: A toe-raising spring assists dorsiflexion in foot drop.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In myositis ossificans traumatica at elbow:

options.A: Forced passive mobilization should not be given
options.B: Forced passive mobilization should be given
options.C: Forced passive mobilization should be given after application of IFT
options.D: Forced passive mobilization should not be given under GA

questions.explanation: Forced passive mobilisation aggravates bleeding and ossification and must be avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: People having following tissue types are more prone to have rheumatic arthritis:
questions.explanation: HLA-DR4 is associated with rheumatoid arthritis; HLA-B27 with ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In talipes equinovarus foot is in: 2A 3B 4 C 5 B 6A 7D 8B 9 A 10 A 11 B 2
questions.explanation: Talipes equinovarus: plantar flexion (equinus) with inversion (varus).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following HLA is positive in ankylosing spondylitis?
questions.explanation: HLA-B27 is positive in about 90% of ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following is true for carpal compression syndrome?
questions.explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome is compression of the median nerve at the wrist.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In the evaluation of an infant, Barlow's provocative test result is positive. This is an indication of:
questions.explanation: A positive Barlow test indicates an unstable (dislocatable) hip.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The primary benefits of CPM after ligament reconstruction is:
questions.explanation: The main benefit of continuous passive motion is reducing adhesion formation and stiffness.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The etiology of periarthritis of shoulder is:

options.C: Fracture of surgical neck of humerus

questions.explanation: Primary adhesive capsulitis is idiopathic.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Erb's palsy is due to injury of:

options.D: Upper roots of brachial plexus involving C5,6

questions.explanation: Erb's palsy is injury to the upper roots (C5-C6) of the brachial plexus.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A man slipped while walking developed swelling immediately in the knee joint. Structure most probably injured is:
questions.explanation: Immediate swelling (haemarthrosis) after a twisting fall most often means an ACL tear.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Ganglion is most commonly seen over:
questions.explanation: A ganglion most commonly arises on the dorsum of the wrist.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: True about Dupuytren's contracture is:

options.B: Palmar nodule is the earliest sign

questions.explanation: A palmar nodule is the earliest sign of Dupuytren's contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: All are common with elbow dislocation except:
questions.explanation: Myositis ossificans progressiva is a genetic disease, not a complication of elbow dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cob's angle is measured in:
questions.explanation: Cobb's angle measures the magnitude of scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Myositis ossificans traumatica is commonest in which of the following joints?
questions.explanation: The elbow is the commonest site of myositis ossificans traumatica.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Myositis ossificans traumatica is most frequent in elbow dislocation in which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: Brachialis is the muscle most often involved after elbow injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The attitude policeman taking tip indicates which of the following?
questions.explanation: The waiter's-tip (policeman's tip) posture indicates Erb's palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Prolonged immobilization can produce all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Prolonged immobilisation causes osteoporosis, stiffness and renal stones, not gallstones.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The basic cause of Volkmann's contracture is:

options.A: Muscle sequestrum formation in flexor policies longus and flexor profundus
options.B: Injury to ulnar and anterior interosseous nerves

questions.explanation: Volkmann's ischaemic contracture results from arterial (vascular) injury leading to muscle ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The finger deformities of Volkmann's ischemic contracture get corrected in which of the following position?
questions.explanation: Finger flexion deformity reduces when the wrist is flexed; extension of the wrist worsens it (key answer concerns wrist position of correction).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayanti Johsi/1st Ed./Pg. 100

questions.question: Post-traumatic avascular necrosis of scaphoid is most common in:
questions.explanation: Avascular necrosis most commonly affects the proximal pole of the scaphoid because blood supply enters distally.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most common nerve damage in shoulder dislocation:
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve is most commonly injured in anterior shoulder dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Earliest visible change in osteoarthritis is:
questions.explanation: Fibrillation of the cartilage surface is the earliest visible change in osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Earliest sign of Volkmann's ischaemic contracture:

options.A: On passive extension there is pain

questions.explanation: Pain on passive extension of the fingers is the earliest sign of Volkmann's ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most commonly the involved structure in Dupuytren's contracture is:
questions.explanation: Pretendinous bands, natatory ligament and others are all involved in Dupuytren's contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The expression knee movements 15-90 degree meant all of the following except:

options.D: Full range of knee movement present

questions.explanation: An arc of 15-90 degrees means a flexion contracture of 15 degrees and flexion limited to 90, so full range is absent.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient diagnosed with an acute posterior cruciate sprain. The mechanism of injury for the posterior cruciate is:

options.A: A forceful landing on the anterior tibia with the knee hyperflexed
options.B: An anteriorly directed force applied to the tibia when the foot is fixed
options.C: A valgus force applied to the knee when the foot is fixed
options.D: Hyperextension, medial rotation of the leg with lateral rotation body

questions.explanation: The PCL is injured by a force to the anterior tibia with the knee flexed, such as a dashboard impact.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with right shoulder adhesive capsulitis is limited to 25 degrees of lateral rotation. Which mobilization technique would be indicated with this limitation?
questions.explanation: To increase lateral rotation, the humeral head is glided anteriorly with lateral distraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient involved in a motor vehicle accident sustains a fracture of the proximal fibula. The fracture damages the motor component of the common peroneal nerve. Exercise Therapy 5 Ankle dorsiflexion and eversion are tested as 2/5. The most appropriate intervention to assist patient with activities of daily living would be:

options.D: An exercise program E. An aquatic program

questions.explanation: Foot drop from common peroneal nerve injury is best managed with an ankle-foot orthosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy 24 hours after a total knee replacement. What exercise would be the most appropriate to begin treatment?
questions.explanation: Quadriceps setting is the appropriate first exercise 24 hours after total knee replacement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 213

questions.question: A patient reports to her therapist that she completely tore one of the ligaments in her ankle. If the patient's comment is accurate, the injury to the ligament should be classified as a:
questions.explanation: A complete ligament tear is a grade III sprain.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Total joint replacements can allow individuals to achieve a significantly higher functional level. What is the primary indication for a total joint replacement?
questions.explanation: Pain is the primary indication for total joint replacement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient scheduled for total hip replacement surgery is referred to physical therapy for preoperative instruction. All of the following should be incorporated into the preoperative session except:

options.B: Gait training with an appropriate assistive device
options.C: Basic precautions for early bed mobility
options.D: Proper use of an adduction pillow

questions.explanation: An adduction pillow is used after surgery, not taught pre-operatively in the same way; the other items are standard pre-op teaching.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 205

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient diagnosed with an Achilles tendon injury. Which clinical finding is not indicative of a ruptured Achilles tendon?

options.C: Lack of toe off during gait
options.D: A palpable defect in the musculotendinous unit

questions.explanation: A negative Thompson test argues against complete rupture; the other findings are typical of rupture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/Pg. 562

questions.question: A patient four weeks status post arthroscopic medial meniscectomy is limited in knee flexion range of motion. Which mobilization technique would be the most beneficial to increase knee flexion?

options.D: Anterior glide of the fibula head

questions.explanation: Posterior tibial glide improves knee flexion (concave tibia on convex femur).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient recovering into the hospital from a total knee replacement is examined by a physical therapist. Assuming an uncomplicated recovery, now much knee range of motion is realistic prior to discharge?
questions.explanation: 0 to 90 degrees of flexion is the realistic range at discharge.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy

Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 213

questions.question: A therapist examines a 40 year old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis. Which clinical finding is not characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.explanation: Heberden's nodes are a feature of osteoarthritis, not rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status post motor vehicle accident is treated using skeletal traction. What bone when fractured is often associated with this type of traction?
questions.explanation: Skeletal traction is classically used for femoral fractures.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient two days status post total hip replacement using a posterolateral approach. The patient is in bed with a sling-pulley system. Which exercise would be inappropriate for the patient assuming an uncomplicated postoperative course?

options.A: Active-assistive abduction and adduction with the thigh supported in the sling
options.B: Active knee flexion and extension in the suspension ling
options.C: Active exercise to the upper extremities

questions.explanation: Active abduction/adduction after posterolateral THR risks dislocation by adduction past midline.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Janant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 208

questions.question: A 25 year old male is diagnosed with a first degree acromioclavicular sprain. The injury occurred two days ago after being checked into the boards while playing hockey. Which of the following would you not expect to be true during the initial examination?

options.A: Increased elevation of the clavicular end of the acromion
options.B: Inability to bring the arm completely across the chest
options.C: Inability to fully abduct the arm throughout the full range of motion
options.D: Point tenderness on palpation of the injury site

questions.explanation: A grade I AC sprain does not produce elevation of the clavicle end; the joint remains stable.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Patella tracking dysfunction is a common problem in orthopedics. Dynamic factors for patella tracking dysfunction include:

options.A: Increase in the angulation between the quadriceps muscle and the patella tendon
options.B: A lateral femoral condyle that is not sufficiently prominent anteriorly

questions.explanation: Vastus medialis obliquus insufficiency is a dynamic cause of poor patellar tracking.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Therapeutic Exercise/Kisner/5th Ed./ Pg. 691,697/711

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient in residual limb wrapping. Which bandage would be the most appropriate to utilize for a patient with a transfemoral amputation?
questions.explanation: A wide (six inch) bandage is used for a transfemoral residual limb.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with an amputation must be competent with residual limb care. The most objective long term goal for bandaging would be:

options.A: The patient will possess general knowledge regarding bandaging of the residual limb
options.B: The patient will attempt to bandage the residual limb twice a day
options.C: The patient will observe three styles of residual limb bandaging
options.D: The patient will perform proper bandaging of the residual limb 100% of the time

questions.explanation: An objective long-term goal is measurable, for example performing proper bandaging 100% of the time.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist reminds a patient of postoperative contraindications following hip replacement surgery. Which statement would not be considered good advice?

options.A: When turning, pivot to the affected side
options.D: Keep a pillow between your legs while sleeping

questions.explanation: Pivoting on the operated leg risks dislocation; patients should take small steps instead.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 208

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy for range of motion and strengthening exercises after sustaining an anterior dislocation of the shoulder. The patient was immobilized in a sling and swathe for four weeks and it has been five weeks since the injury date. Which activity would be the most appropriate for the patient to begin strengthening of the involved shoulder?

options.A: Medial and lateral rotation in sidelying with two pound weights within the available range of motion
options.B: Medial and lateral rotation using elastic tubing with the arm at the patient's side and elbow at 90 degrees
options.C: Isokinetic medial and lateral rotation at speeds less than 120 degrees per second
options.D: Isometric strengthening exercise with the arm positioned at the patient's side

questions.explanation: Five weeks after an anterior dislocation, rehabilitation starts with isometrics at the side before loaded or end-range work.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 2

questions.question: A 36-year-old female is limited to 30 degrees of lateral rotation at the right shoulder. Which shoulder mobilization technique would be the most beneficial to increase lateral rotation?

options.A: Anterior glide of the humeral head
options.B: Posterior glide of the humeral head
options.C: Inferior glide of the humeral head
options.D: Superior glide of the humeral head

questions.explanation: Lateral rotation is increased by anterior glide of the humeral head.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which progressive resistive exercise would function to strengthen the infraspinatus and teres minor?

options.A: Extension of the shoulder with dumbbell weights
options.B: Flexion of the shoulder with dumbbell weights
options.C: Lateral rotation of the shoulder with elastic tubing
options.D: Medial rotation of the shoulder with elastic truing

questions.explanation: Lateral rotation against resistance strengthens infraspinatus and teres minor.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a transfemoral amputation begins gait training with prosthesis. What effect will a hip flexion contracture have on the patient's gait?

options.A: The patient will demonstrate increased stability in the prosthetic knee
options.B: The patient's step length on the prosthetic side will be increased.
options.C: The hip flexion contracture will not affect the patient's gait pattern
options.D: The patient will not begin to ambulate until normal range of motion is restored

questions.explanation: A hip flexion contracture shortens the step of the opposite limb and affects prosthetic stability and step length.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Tidy's Physiotherapy/KM Varghese/12th Ed./Pg. 269

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with a suspected acutely torn medial meniscus. Which symptom is not commonly associated with a medial meniscus tear?

options.A: Tenderness along the medial point line

questions.explanation: Hamstring atrophy is not a feature of a medial meniscus tear (quadriceps atrophy is).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 14 year old girl presents with a twenty-five degree left thoracic scoliotic curvature. All of the following are appropriate immediate forms of treatment except:
questions.explanation: A 25 degree curve in a growing child is managed with bracing and exercise rather than surgery.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When wrapping the residual limb of a patient with a transfemoral amputation a therapist should adhere to all of the following except:

options.A: The bandage should provide increased pressure proximally
options.B: The bandage should be smooth and wrinkle free
options.C: The bandage should be applied using diagonal turns
options.D: The bandage should be applied to encourage proximal joint extension

questions.explanation: Pressure should be greatest distally and decrease proximally, never greater proximally.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a 67 year old female, four weeks status post total hip replacement in a home exercise Exercise Therapy 9 program. Which exercise description would be inappropriate for the patient?

options.A: Lie on your involved side and lift the involved leg towards the ceiling.
options.B: Place a rolled up towel under your knee. Rest the weight of the thigh on the towel roll. Lift the heel off the table so that you straighten the knee.
options.C: Lie on your back with the opposite knee bent. Tighten the thigh muscle, keeping the leg straight and lift the leg toward the ceiling
options.D: Lie on your back with knees bent. Raise you buttocks off the table

questions.explanation: Side-lying with the operated leg uppermost lifting it (abduction) is not appropriate early because of the positioning and abduction load; other exercises are safe.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/Elesiver/1st Ed./Pg. 208

questions.question: A 16-year-old basketball player is anxious to return to athletic competition following rehabilitation from an Achilles tendon rupture. The athlete is objectively ready to return to competition, however continues to demonstrate a severe preoccupation with reinjury. The most appropriate response is the:

options.A: Allow the patient to return to basketball without restriction
options.B: Information patient that he should not participate in basketball this season
options.C: Design a functional progression for basketball which allows the patient to progress to higher level activities in a gradual fashion
options.D: Discuss other less demanding athletic activities with the patient

questions.explanation: A graded functional progression back to sport addresses fear of reinjury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 562-563

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy after sustaining a colles' fracture. A Colles' fracture refers to an injury of the:
questions.explanation: Colles' fracture is a fracture of the distal radius.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient two weeks status post transtibial amputation is instructed by his physician to remain at rest for two days after contracting bronchitis. The most appropriate position for the patient in bed is:

options.A: Supine with a pillow under the patient's knees
options.B: Supine with a pillow under the patient's thigh and knee

questions.explanation: Legs are kept extended to prevent knee flexion contracture; pillows under the knee are avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 231

questions.question: A 21-year-old male suffers a primary dislocation of the right shoulder playing football. The athlete is referred to physical therapy after three weeks of immobilization. A physical therapist might elect to begin treatment with all of the following except:
questions.explanation: High-speed isokinetic exercise is too aggressive for a recently immobilised shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 79, 81

questions.question: A therapist identifies excessive femoral neck anteversion during an examination of a patient diagnosed with trochanteric bursitis. This structural finding commonly results in:

options.A: An increase in hip lateral rotation
options.B: An increase in hip medial rotation

questions.explanation: Excess femoral anteversion increases hip medial rotation and causes in-toeing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/ 3rd Ed./Pg. 323

questions.question: The most common mechanism for an anterior talofibular ligament sprain is:
questions.explanation: ATFL injury results from inversion with plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/Pg. 556

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy diagnosed with right hip trochanteric bursitis. Which clinical finding is usually not associated with trochanteric bursitis?

options.B: Full hip active range of motion
options.D: Joint play motions are limited in a capsular pattern

questions.explanation: Trochanteric bursitis does not produce a capsular pattern of the hip joint.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 33

questions.question: A patient status post large rotator cuff repair surgery is referred to physical therapy. Which of the following motions would you initially expect to be the most restricted?
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation is protected and most restricted after large cuff repair.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 478 -479

questions.question: A 15-year-old boy has pain over the tibial tubercle and clinically very prominent. The pain has been for 4 months with no history of injury and systemic illness. He most probably has:
questions.explanation: A prominent painful tibial tubercle in an adolescent is Osgood-Schlatter disease.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The carpal tunnel located on the volar aspect of the wrist contains:
questions.explanation: The carpal tunnel contains nine flexor tendons and the median nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a history of rheumatoid arthritis is referred to physical therapy diagnosed with acute glenohumeral joint pain. Which treatment technique would be inappropriate for the patient?

options.A: Passive range of motion in pain free range

questions.explanation: Grade III-IV mobilisation is inappropriate in an acutely inflamed rheumatoid joint.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The tendon of the ____________ muscle is commonly compressed against the bottom of the acromion process in a patient diagnosed with impingement syndrome?
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus is compressed beneath the acromion in impingement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 477

questions.question: Bed positioning is important for patient's status post amputation. The prone position or prone lying is re- commended for thirty minutes several times a day. This position is of particular importance for ______ amputations?
questions.explanation: Prone lying prevents hip flexion contracture, mainly important in transfemoral amputation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 231

questions.question: A physical therapist observes a patient with a transfemoral amputation during gait training. The therapist identifies marked lateral rotation of the prosthesis at heel strike. Which of the following would not be a contributing factor to the patient's gait deviation?

options.C: Excessive toe-out built into the prosthesis

questions.explanation: A short prosthesis does not cause lateral rotation at heel strike; toe-out, poor suspension and weak medial rotators do.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/Elesiver/1st Ed./Pg. 244

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient diagnosed with rotator cuff tendonitis in transverse plane resistive exercises. Which motions would be appropriate based on the given information?
questions.explanation: Rotation exercises are transverse-plane motions at the shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 480

questions.question: A therapist develops a physical therapy problem list after competing an initial examination on a patient diagnosed with right shoulder impingement. Which of the following entries would not typically belong in the physical therapy problem list?

options.A: Decreased active right shoulder lateral rotation
options.B: Decreased strength of the right upper trapezius and middle deltoid
options.C: Increased pain with right shoulder active movement
options.D: Increased stress secondary to financial problems

questions.explanation: Financial stress is not a physical therapy problem-list item for shoulder impingement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which clinical observation is not usually characteristic with a rotator cuff tear?

options.A: The patient is less than 40 years old
options.B: The patient is often unable to move the arm actively without pain
options.D: Night pain is a common patient complaint

questions.explanation: Cuff tears are uncommon below 40 years without major trauma.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 478

questions.question: Earliest sign of Volkmann's ischemic contracture is:
questions.explanation: Pain is the earliest sign of Volkmann's ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Claw hand is seen in:
questions.explanation: Claw hand is characteristic of ulnar nerve injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Nerve abscess is seen in the .......... nerve.
questions.explanation: Nerve abscess in leprosy is commonest in the ulnar nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Tardy ulnar nerve palsy is due to:

options.B: Fixation of nerve in the groove by osteoarthritis

questions.explanation: Cubitus valgus stretches the ulnar nerve over years and causes tardy ulnar palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Myositis ossificans is commonly seen at in the......... joint:
questions.explanation: The elbow is the commonest joint associated with myositis ossificans.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Calcification of menisci is seen in:
questions.explanation: Meniscal calcification (chondrocalcinosis) is a feature of pseudogout.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Distance from the knee joint in below knee amputation is......inches.
questions.explanation: The standard below-knee residual limb length is about 5.5 inches below the knee joint line.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Myositis ossificans is most common around the joint:
questions.explanation: Myositis ossificans is most common around the elbow.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In De Quervain's syndrome the following tendons are inflamed:

options.A: Extensor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
options.B: Extensor carpi radialis longus and opponens
options.C: Extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus
options.D: Abductor pollicis and extensor carpi radialis brevis

questions.explanation: De Quervain's involves extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Commonest site of myositis ossificans traumatica is:
questions.explanation: Brachialis is the commonest site of myositis ossificans traumatica.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The mallet finger results from injury to:

options.D: Extensor tendons of the terminal phalanx of finger

questions.explanation: Mallet finger is injury to the extensor tendon at the terminal phalanx.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Painful arc syndrome is due to:
questions.explanation: Chronic supraspinatus tendinitis, subacromial bursitis and greater tuberosity fracture can all cause a painful arc.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Maximum weight used for skin traction is:
questions.explanation: Skin traction is limited to about 5 kg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Treatment of acute myositis ossificans is:
questions.explanation: Acute myositis ossificans is treated by rest and immobilisation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Tardy ulnar nerve palsy is seen with:
questions.explanation: Old lateral humeral condyle fracture causes cubitus valgus and tardy ulnar palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Medial meniscal tear is more common than that of lateral meniscus tear because of its decreased:
questions.explanation: The medial meniscus tears more often because it is less mobile.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Total Claw hand is caused by injury to:
questions.explanation: Total claw hand occurs with combined ulnar and median nerve injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Trigger finger is most likely to be associated with:
questions.explanation: Trigger finger is associated with diabetes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Pointing index is due to:

options.D: Injury to flexor digitorum profundus tendon

questions.explanation: Pointing index follows median nerve injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Treatment in the early stage of myositis ossifican is:
questions.explanation: Early myositis ossificans is treated by immobilisation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most common complication of Colle's fracture is:
questions.explanation: Stiffness of the fingers is the commonest complication of Colles' fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most common complication of clavicle fracture is:
questions.explanation: Shoulder stiffness is the commonest complication after a clavicle fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Disease where distal interphalangeal joint is characteristically involved:
questions.explanation: Psoriatic arthritis characteristically involves the distal interphalangeal joints.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Herbeden's nodules are seen in:
questions.explanation: Heberden nodes (DIP) are a feature of osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Commonest degenerative joint disease is:
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis is the commonest degenerative joint disease.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The following are radiological signs of Paget's disease of bone except:
questions.explanation: Paget disease shows cotton-wool skull, picture-frame vertebra and blade-of-grass lesions; hair-on-end is a feature of thalassaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Turek's SL, Lippincot Raven/Pg. 737-738

questions.question: The following is true of spondylolisthesis:
questions.explanation: Spondylolisthesis is forward slip of one vertebra (usually L5 on S1) associated with a defect of the pars/posterior arch.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Beheaded Scottish Terrier sign is seen in:
questions.explanation: On oblique lumbar views a collar on the Scottie dog (pars defect) indicates spondylolysis, and a 'decapitated' dog indicates spondylolisthesis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A postoperative rigid dressing provides a patient status post amputation with all of the following advantages except:

options.A: Allows for daily inspection and dressing changes
options.B: Allows for earlier ambulation with a pylon attachment
options.D: Reduces the length of time necessary for shrinking of the limb

questions.explanation: A rigid dressing limits oedema and allows early pylon ambulation but, unlike a soft dressing, does not allow daily inspection of the wound.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status post total hip replacement indicates to her therapist that she was instructed to avoid hip flexion greater than 90 degrees, adduction, and medial rotation. The most likely sum approach utilized by the surgeon is:
questions.explanation: Avoiding flexion beyond 90 degrees, adduction and internal rotation is the precaution for the posterolateral approach.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The boutonniere deformity of finger is characterized by:

options.A: Inability to completely extend PIP joint
options.B: Inability to completely flex PIP joint
options.D: Inability to completely flex MP joint

questions.explanation: Boutonniere deformity is PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension from central slip rupture; the PIP cannot be fully extended.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Piriformis syndrome is caused by piriformis muscle that compresses:
questions.explanation: Piriformis syndrome results from compression of the sciatic nerve by the piriformis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Following THR the following position of the hip joint is avoided:
questions.explanation: After a posterior-approach total hip replacement flexion beyond 90 degrees with adduction and internal rotation is avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The artificial limb prosthesis is most satisfactory in which of the following amputations:
questions.explanation: A below-knee (transtibial) prosthesis gives the best functional results.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist begins prosthetic training activities for a patient with a transtibial amputation. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial activity?
questions.explanation: Weight shifting in standing (to learn loading the prosthesis) is the first step of transtibial prosthetic training.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Tennis elbow is:
questions.explanation: Tennis elbow is lateral epicondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The most common site at disc prolapse is:
questions.explanation: L4-L5 is the commonest level of lumbar disc herniation (with L5-S1).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The most common cause of acute sciatica is due to:

options.B: Secondaries of spine Model Question Paper - 1 123

questions.explanation: Acute prolapse of a lumbar intervertebral disc is the commonest cause of acute sciatica.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Consider the following statements about carpal tunnel syndrome. 1. It may occur in acromegaly 2. It may occur in pregnancy 3. It causes delayed ulnar nerve conduction 4. It may be associated with wasting of abductor pollicis. Of these statements:
questions.explanation: CTS is associated with acromegaly and pregnancy and causes wasting of abductor pollicis brevis from median nerve compression; it does not affect ulnar conduction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Dowager's hump is a kyphosis condition that is found most often in:
questions.explanation: Dowager's hump is thoracic kyphosis from vertebral compression fractures in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The nerve involved in carpal tunnel syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome is compression of the median nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The level of the constricting nodule in case of Trigger finger is at:

options.A: Neck of the corresponding metacarpal bone

questions.explanation: The constricting nodule/stenosis in trigger finger is at the A1 pulley over the metacarpophalangeal joint.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cervical spondylosis is more common at:
questions.explanation: Cervical spondylosis most often affects C5-C6 and C6-C7.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Osteophytes developing at the joint, characteristically compresses spinal nerves at:
questions.explanation: Osteophytes at the uncovertebral and facet joints narrow the intervertebral foramen and compress the spinal nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Trigger finger is:

options.A: A feature at carpal tunnel syndrome
options.B: Injury to fingers while operating a gun
options.C: Stenosis tenovaginitis of flexor tendon or affected finger

questions.explanation: Trigger finger is stenosing tenosynovitis (tenovaginitis) of the flexor tendon sheath.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cervical spondylosis:

options.A: Most frequently results from an incidence of acute trauma.
options.B: Causes compression of nerve roots to produce an upper motor neuro lesion in the lower limbs.
options.C: Produces pain and paraesthesia over the lateral aspect at the forearm and thumb when affecting the 6th cervical nerve.
options.D: Most frequently affects the upper cervical vertebral

questions.explanation: C6 root involvement gives pain and paraesthesia over the lateral forearm and thumb.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Wartenberg's sign is:

options.A: Abduction of little finger with loss of intrinsics
options.B: Adduction of little finger with loss of intrinsics
options.C: Abduction of ring finger with loss of intrinsics
options.D: Abduction of little finger without loss of intrinsics

questions.explanation: Wartenberg sign is abduction of the little finger due to unopposed extensor digiti minimi with ulnar intrinsic weakness.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In spondylolisthesis, there is fracture of vertebra in:

options.B: Pars interarticularis of the neural arch

questions.explanation: Spondylolisthesis (spondylolysis) involves a defect in the pars interarticularis of the neural arch.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cobb's angle is measured for:
questions.explanation: The Cobb angle measures the severity of scoliosis on a standing X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The most important single special investigation in lumbar disc prolapse is:
questions.explanation: MRI is the investigation of choice for lumbar disc prolapse.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cock-up splint is used in:
questions.explanation: A cock-up splint holds the wrist in extension in radial nerve palsy (wrist drop).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The Milwaukee brace is used to for correction of:
questions.explanation: The Milwaukee brace (CTLSO) is used to treat scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following prosthesis (cervical) movement best controlled at the cervical spine:
questions.explanation: The halo-vest orthosis gives the most rigid control of the cervical spine.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Common vertebral level of spondylolisthesis is:
questions.explanation: Isthmic spondylolisthesis most commonly occurs at L5-S1.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which splint is prescribed for claw hand deformity?
questions.explanation: A knuckle-bender (lumbrical bar) splint prevents MCP hyperextension in claw hand.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Therapeutic Exercise Fundation/Kisner/ 5th Ed./Pg. 597

questions.question: Lateral wedging is given to correct:
questions.explanation: A lateral heel/sole wedge shifts load medially and is used in genu varum.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essentials of Orthopedics and Applied Physiotherapy/

Jayant Joshi/Pg. 344

questions.question: Spondylosis is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Spondylosis causes a stiff spine from degenerative changes and osteophytes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Volkman's ischemic contracture the muscle commonly involved is:
questions.explanation: Flexor digitorum profundus is the muscle most commonly involved in Volkmann's ischaemic contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: What is the position of immobilization in fracture of both bones of the forearm in an adult male?
questions.explanation: Both-bone forearm fractures in adults are immobilised in mid-prone (neutral rotation).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A football player, while playing, twists his knee over the ankle. He still continues to play. After 2 days he noticed painful swelling of the knee joint. The diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: A twisting knee injury with delayed painful swelling suggests an ACL tear (haemarthrosis).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: If the greater tuberosity of the humerus is lost, which of the following movements will be affected?
questions.explanation: The greater tuberosity carries supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor, so abduction and lateral rotation are affected.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A lady present with a history of fracture radius, which was put on plaster of paris cast for 4 weeks. After that she developed swelling of hands with shiny skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Rupture of extensor pollicis longus tendon

questions.explanation: A swollen, shiny hand after cast removal for a radius fracture is reflex sympathetic dystrophy (CRPS).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which pain is improving with exercise?
questions.explanation: The pain of ankylosing spondylitis improves with exercise and worsens with rest.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: An adult sustained a fracture of the both bones of mid forearm at the same level. After manipulation the position of immobilisation of the forearm in the plaster would be:
questions.explanation: After manipulation both-bone forearm fractures are immobilised in mid-prone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Rheumatoid arthritis can cause many symptoms in its later stages. Which of the following symptoms would most likely be common in a patient who has had rheumatoid arthritis for a long period of time?
questions.explanation: Long-standing rheumatoid arthritis causes ulnar deviation of the fingers.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: You are treating a patient who is complaining of right shoulder pain. The patient has been diagnosed with a frozen adhesive capsulated shoulder. Which of the following would describe the capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint?
questions.explanation: The glenohumeral capsular pattern is external rotation, then abduction, then internal rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a vertebral artery test on a patient prior to using traction and mobilization techniques in upper cervical spine. During the test the patient begins to demonstrate nystagmus and blurred vision. The therapist should:

options.A: Repeat the vertebral artery test to confirm the original results
options.B: Proceed cautiously with traction and mobilization techniques in the upper cervical spine
options.C: Avoid traction or mobilization techniques in the upper cervical spine
options.D: Discharge the patient from physical therapy

questions.explanation: Nystagmus and blurred vision during the vertebral artery test mean upper cervical traction or mobilisation must be avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopaedic Physical Assessment/Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 171

questions.question: All of the following are true concerning scoliosis except:

options.A: A 15 degree to 20 degree curve is mild curve
options.B: Bracing is an effective treatment tool
options.C: Scoliosis is named by the direction of concavity

questions.explanation: Scoliosis is named by the side of the convexity of the curve, not the concavity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: ____splint is prescribed for a case of median nerve injury.
questions.explanation: A short opponens splint holds the thumb in opposition for median nerve palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Enthesopathy occurs in ________ .
questions.explanation: Enthesitis (inflammation at tendon/ligament insertions) is characteristic of ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Lumbar spine is not involved in ________ .
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis tends to spare the lumbar spine, unlike osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopaedics and Applied Physiotherapy/Jayant joshi/ 1st Ed./Pg. 305

questions.question: Which of the following spinal orthosis controls LS flexion-extension
questions.explanation: The Knight spinal orthosis restricts lumbosacral flexion and extension.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In supraspinatus tendinitis the painful arc syndrome ranges from:
questions.explanation: The painful arc of supraspinatus tendinitis is about 60 to 120 degrees of abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Positive rose water test is suggestive of:
questions.explanation: The Rose-Waaler (rose water) test is positive in rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Radiologically bamboo spine sign is seen in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bamboo spine on X-ray is characteristic of ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Ape thumb deformity is produced by injury to which of the following nerves?
questions.explanation: Median nerve injury causes ape-hand (flat thenar) deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Mallet finger is produced in which of the following injuries?

options.A: Avulsion of extensor tendon at the base of middle phalanx
options.B: Avulsion of flexor profundus tendon at the base of terminal phalanx
options.C: Avulsion of extensor tendon at the base of terminal phalanx

questions.explanation: Mallet finger is avulsion of the extensor tendon at the base of the terminal phalanx.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Krukenberg's amputation is done for problems of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Krukenberg's operation converts the forearm stump into a pincer in bilateral hand loss.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Pointing Index sign is seen in nerve:
questions.explanation: Pointing index follows median nerve injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The acronym HARM used for the management of acute sports injuries stands for:

options.B: Help to ambulate with rapid motion Exercise Therapy
options.C: Do not use heat, alcohol, running and massage
options.D: Hot packs, aerobics, resisted exercises and mobilization

questions.explanation: HARM: avoid Heat, Alcohol, Running and Massage in acute injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with shoulder pain of unknown etiology is referred by his physician for magnetic resonance imaging. Results of the test reveal a partial tear of the infraspinatus muscle. Which muscle group would you expect to be the most seriously affected by the injury?
questions.explanation: Infraspinatus is a lateral rotator of the shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: BD Chaurasia, Human Anatomy/Exercise Therapy/

4th Ed./Pg. 146

questions.question: Bamboo spine is seen in:
questions.explanation: Bamboo spine is a feature of ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The open basket weave taping technique is commonly used as a form of treatment for an acute ankle sprain. Which of the following does not accurately describe the benefits of the open basketweave taping technique?

options.A: Allows freedom of movement in dorsiflexion
options.B: Allows freedom of movement in plantar flexion

questions.explanation: The open basket-weave technique allows room for oedema, so that is a benefit; option C is described as not a benefit in the source key.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 26-year-old male involved in a motorcycle accident sustains a T10 vertebral fracture. The patient's physician attempts to restrict forward thoracic flexion by using an externally applied device. Which of the following would be the most appropriate selection?
questions.explanation: A thoracolumbosacral orthosis limits thoracic flexion after a T10 fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Median nerve injury above elbow leads to:
questions.explanation: High median nerve injury causes ape thumb deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 650

questions.question: A physical therapist reviews a physician's examination of a patient that will be seen in therapy later in the day. The examination identifies excessive medial displacement of the elbow during ligamentous testing. Which ligament is typically involved in medial instability of the elbow?
questions.explanation: The ulnar collateral ligament prevents medial instability of the elbow.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 266

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient with limited range of motion at the glenohumeral joint. Which of the following is considered a capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint?

options.A: Greatest limitation in flexion flowed by medial rotation
options.B: Greatest limitation in lateral rotation, followed by abduction
options.C: Greatest limitation in medial rotation, followed by abduction
options.D: Greatest limitation in extension and lateral rotation

questions.explanation: The glenohumeral capsular pattern is lateral rotation, then abduction, then medial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/ 5th Ed./Pg. 253

questions.question: Muscles involved in Volkman's ischemic contracture:
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus, profundus and sublimis can all be involved.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopedics and Applied

Physiotherapy/Jayant Joshi/Reprint 2009/

Elsevier/Pg. 99

questions.question: Medial meniscus is more vulnerable to injury because of:

options.A: Its fixity to tibial colateral ligament

questions.explanation: The medial meniscus is vulnerable because it is fixed to the tibial collateral ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Clumsiness of the hand in case of leprosy is due to involvement of:

options.D: Flexor carpi radialis Biomechanics of L/L

questions.explanation: Clumsiness in leprosy is due to interosseous muscle paralysis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Hip joint is weakest in which of the following attitudes?
questions.explanation: The hip is weakest in flexion, adduction and internal rotation (dislocation position).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Kinesiology of Musculoskeletal System/Neuman/Pg. 400

questions.question: The most common type of contracture in a patient with a transfemoral amputation is:
questions.explanation: Hip flexion contracture is the commonest contracture in transfemoral amputation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopedicss/Jayant Joshi/Reprint 2009/Pg. 236

questions.question: A patient with a transfemoral amputation is referred to physical therapy for gait training. During the initial examination the therapist identifies lateral trunk bending towards the affected side during the stance phase of gait. A possible cause of this deviation is:

options.C: The socket diameter is too small
options.D: There is an increased amount of edema in the residual limb

questions.explanation: Lateral trunk bending toward the prosthetic side in stance can be caused by a prosthesis that is too short, an abducted socket, weak abductors or pain.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist observes excessive knee flexion from heel strike to midstance while observing patient with a transtibial amputation during gait training. A possible cause for this deviation is:

options.A: The foot is set in neutral
options.B: The socket is set posterior in relation to the foot
options.D: The socket is aligned in excessive flexion

questions.explanation: Excessive knee flexion at heel strike to mid-stance in a transtibial prosthesis is due to excessive socket flexion, a dorsiflexed foot or a stiff heel.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Distal interphalangeal joint is not involved in:
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis typically spares the distal interphalangeal joints, unlike osteoarthritis and psoriatic arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Para-articular erosions are most commonly seen in:
questions.explanation: Marginal (para-articular) erosions at the bare areas are characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
